rationale: Both documents credit White-Bear Steering (Raman et al. 2026) by name as the basis the method deviates from, describing the same two innovations: a think-vs-suppress contrast instead of think/don't-think, and prefix-only positioning instead of WBS's tested all-positions/read-cell/context-only. The closing message, however, adds several specifics about the source not present in the write-up — that WBS 'explicitly excluded the suppress items', that WBS found 'a narrow useful dose window', and it frames the two contributions under explicit 'Novel contrast'/'Novel position' headers, a more assertive novelty framing than the write-up's comparatively measured 'Where it came from' narrative.
